label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
**4 out of 5 stars**

We bought the Lindqvist Optics PT-20 from Chancel AV in February 2026 for $2,140, plus $95 for the wall mount. It replaced the webcam we had been using to livestream worship since 2020. I would buy it again, but that is a lot of money for a small church, and a congregation under 100 might do just fine with something less expensive.

Our nave is 92 feet long, and the camera is mounted on the balcony rail at the back. The 20x optical zoom lets us get a useful view of the pulpit and other parts of the chancel from that distance. The picture is 1080p60, and it has both NDI HX and plain HDMI out. It also uses PoE, which meant one cable up to the balcony. We run it into OBS on an old office PC and stream to our YouTube channel, where we usually have 30 to 60 viewers on a Sunday.

We have nine presets stored: altar, pulpit, lectern, font, choir loft, piano, a wide view, and two for the chancel steps. Erik, our 16-year-old acolyte, runs the camera from the free web app on a tablet. He learned it in one afternoon.

Setup was not entirely smooth. On the first Sunday, the presets had drifted a few degrees by the time we got to the sermon. A firmware update to version 2.4 in March fixed that. The autofocus also tends to hunt when someone walks between the camera and the pulpit, so we lock the focus on the presets.

The manual is thin and badly translated, which did not help when we were trying to sort things out. Chancel AV’s phone support was much better. Marcy was excellent and helped us get through it without making us feel foolish.

The picture has been a real improvement. During the Easter Vigil in April, we sang the first “Christ the Lord Is Risen Today” with only candles lit. The picture got grainy, but it stayed usable. With our old webcam, we would have seen little more than dots. Delores, who is 82 and homebound, called to say she could finally read the hymn numbers on the board. That meant more to me than any list of specifications.

One important limit: this camera did nothing for our sound problem. Audio is not the camera’s job, and if people at home cannot hear the service well, a better picture will not fix that.

For us, the zoom, presets and improved picture made the purchase worthwhile. I would encourage another small parish to look honestly at its room, its budget and what it is trying to fix before spending this much.
